newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.0/11.0 percent on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity was ample and operators were expecting a similar condition on Thursday following central bank buying of some $400 million to support the dollar on Tuesday.

But operators said they feared a possible tightening of liquidity on Friday on market talk of maturing short-term papers (SBPUs) of around 800 billion rupiah and another 200 billion rupiah of maturing central bank repo papers (SBIs).
However, the figures could not be confirmed.
One local bank dealer said, however, the maturing papers would offset the rupiah injection.
One foreign bank dealer said the ample liquidity on Wednesday was not surprising one day after bank liquidity reports.
Overnight swap also fell below the 0.5 points level to 0.4/0.5 points. Tom/next was quoted at 0.55/0.60.
Dealers said the interbank rates remained low depsite some buying from some state banks in the morning.
Longer-term money had eased on the back of ample short-term market, they said. One-wek money eased to 13.75/14.0 percent and one-month money to 14.50/14.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 13.80 percent, compared with 16.01 percent on Monday.
